jobs.prompt:
chore(cpp): bring three reviewed follow-ups into the delivered native gateway branch

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the delivered native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). Three reviewed branches must be merged into it. Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body (short, plain language: what each follow-up brings, what you had to reconcile, what was verified).

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev` gives a toolchain that builds this tree (the CI workflow shows the exact package list and how it builds the pinned SQLite: do the same). The environment has `CCACHE_DIR` set to a directory that is restored before and saved after your job; `ccache` is installed.


RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Tests use local mocks only.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each merge and each fix, keep a checklist in `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-combine-3-20261120.md`, read it and `git log` first after a restart. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes; the repository's hosted CI runs the full matrix when your branch is pushed, so do not run full four-shard suites yourself.
- Ordinary merge commits only (`git fetch origin <branch>` then `git merge --no-ff`): never squash or rebase. Do not delete or weaken tests.

TASK
Merge, in this order:
1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-macos-final-20261119-44637373710-1`: Apple Silicon confirmation (documentation and one Darwin-conditional test expectation). No conflicts expected.
2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-stream-retry-20261119-44629153076-1`: the gateway retries an upstream stream that fails before any output (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-stream-retry-20261119.md`). No conflicts expected.
3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-build-cache-20261119-44628404886-1`: compiler cache for the build driver, fuzz builder, packagers and CI workflows (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-build-cache-20261119.md`). It conflicts with your branch in `cpp/gateway/packaging/macos/build.py` and `cpp/gateway/packaging/portable/Dockerfile` (possibly `packaging/portable/build.sh`, `tools/macos-build.sh`): your branch added the binding of the full release commit into the build (`UOS_PACKAGE_GIT_COMMIT`, so health reports the real commit; tests `tests/release_identity_test.cpp`, `tests/health_test.cpp`), the cache branch added the compiler launcher and a dependencies stage. BOTH must survive: packaged builds bind the commit AND compile through the launcher when one is configured; the release-package workflow still does not restore a cache. Because the commit hash is a compile definition, make sure it does not defeat the cache for every other translation unit: only the translation unit(s) that use `UOS_PACKAGE_GIT_COMMIT` may receive that definition (check how your branch passes it; if it is passed to all compiles, restrict it to `src/release.cpp` and anything else that actually reads it) and show with `ccache --show-stats` that two package-style builds at different commits share hits for everything else.
Then verify: `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`; `actionlint` on both workflows; build with the launcher and run the release-identity, health, startup, Codex routing/stream-retry (`kv_budget_part1_test`, `codex_serial_routing_http_test`, `serve_delivery_http_test`) and Gemini tests in release; one portable package build plus verifier in the background if Docker is available, confirming health reports the built commit.

DONE WHEN
All three merges are in with preserved ancestry, both features work together as described, and the checks pass.
